answer: A stake-backed reputation registry resists Sybil attacks by making identity expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, so spawning a thousand hollow accounts costs a thousand deposits. The deposit is ferrous — hard to fake and slow to withdraw — and it is slashed when peers report fraud. Honest work builds a public record, so a new account has no echo of past reliability and earns trust only gradually. An attacker can buy one identity, but buying an army of trusted ones costs more than the fraud is worth.
